claims.evidence: No output file exists; nothing structured was produced.

uncertainties: No transcript captured for the baseline, so the exact content and number of clarifying questions cannot be verified — only inferred from empty outputs + short timing.

suggestions.reason: No transcript was captured for the baseline run, so the only verifiable signal is 'no output file + short run'. Several behavioral assertions (which clarifying question, how many, whether it targets scope) are unverifiable without a transcript. Capturing the assistant's text response for no-file runs would let the dialogue-behavior assertions be graded on evidence rather than inference.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to save/persist the output — suggests librarian skill instead
suggestions.reason: This assertion conflates two things (don't save AND recommend librarian). A baseline that produces nothing passes the 'don't save' half trivially while failing the meaningful 'suggest librarian' half. Splitting it into two assertions would make the comparison between skill and baseline cleaner.

eval_feedback.overall: The baseline naturally clarifies-first (the one passing behavioral assertion), which is the expected human-like default — but it produces no structured artifact and has no awareness of the depth model, researcher, or librarian skills. This is the intended contrast: the skill turns an ad-hoc clarify-and-stop into a complete, structured breakdown. Capturing baseline transcripts would strengthen grading of the behavioral assertions.
